findings.reason: a worker implementing this literally either breaks an existing admission the section claims to leave unchanged, or has to guess whether `claim_disposition` supplements or replaces `stopped_with_terminal_manifest`; the plan must say that only the waiting-phase decision moves to `claim_disposition` (leaving the stopped-peer test in place, or adding a case for it) or the section ships a regression its own done-when cannot see.
findings.text: the deliverable says the walk "calls `claim_disposition` for each peer claim", while (a) `reckon/crew/promotion_scope.py` contains zero occurrences of `claim_disposition` at 401a2151eb, so this describes the fix as an existing fact, and (b) judging the whole walk by `claim_disposition` narrows the stopped-peer branch: `stopped_with_terminal_manifest` (`reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py:2048-2093`) admits a stopped peer on liveness plus a fresh terminal manifest alone, whereas `claim_disposition` (`reckon/crew/node.py:1534-1576`) binds the same peer when `unintegrated_claim_work` finds a commit past its base (`reckon/crew/node.py:1456-1465`), so `tests/test_a_stopped_runs_claim_does_not_block_another_landing.py:194` — a stopped peer whose worktree holds its own commit and whose manifest reads `complete`, expected to be admitted — would be refused, and the section's three cases do not cover it
